let's create a new branch and investigate the dependabot vulns

I'll branch off an up-to-date `main`, then pull the actual Dependabot alerts and inspect the dependency files.

Now on `chore/dependabot-vulns` (off up-to-date `main`). Let me pull the actual Dependabot alerts and inspect the dependency manifest.

Clear picture — all 3 are **dev-tooling, Windows-only** vulnerabilities in the build chain:

| # | Sev | Package | Issue | Vulnerable | Patched |
|---|-----|---------|-------|-----------|---------|
| 2 | **High** | vite | `server.fs.deny` bypass (Windows alt paths) | ≤ 7.3.4 | **7.3.5** |
| 3 | Medium | vite (launch-editor) | NTLMv2 hash disclosure via UNC (Windows) | ≤ 7.3.4 | **7.3.5** |
| 1 | Low | esbuild | arbitrary file read, dev server (Windows) | < 0.28.1 | **0.28.1** |

Let me check the currently-resolved versions and how `esbuild` is pulled in.

Current resolved: **vite 7.3.3** and **esbuild 0.27.7** — both vulnerable. Note vite pins `esbuild ^0.27.0`, but the esbuild fix is only in **0.28.1** (outside that range), so I need to confirm whether a patched vite widens the esbuild range. Let me query the registry.

vite's latest 7.x is **7.3.6** (patches both vite CVEs) but still pins `esbuild ^0.27.0`, so esbuild won't reach the patched **0.28.1** on vite 7 without an override. The clean path for esbuild may be vite 8. Let me check vite 8's esbuild range, Node engine requirement, and whether this repo even has a custom vite config.

Key finding: **vite 7.3.6 widened its esbuild range to `^0.27.0 || ^0.28.0`** (7.3.5 was still `^0.27.0`). So a bump to **vite 7.3.6** lets esbuild resolve to the patched **0.28.x** — fixing all three alerts within vite 7.x, no major upgrade or `overrides` needed. Let me establish a baseline audit, then apply the bump.

Baseline confirmed: 2 vulnerabilities (the audit groups both vite advisories), and latest esbuild is **0.28.1** (patched). Now I'll bump the vite floor to `^7.3.6` in package.json (documents intent + sets a patched minimum) and reinstall.

vite is now **7.3.6** (both vite CVEs resolved), but esbuild stayed at 0.27.7 — a plain install won't jump it across the `|| ^0.28.0` boundary since 0.27.7 still satisfies the range. Now that vite permits `^0.28.0`, `npm audit fix` can bump it cleanly. Let me run it.

All three resolved — **vite 7.3.6**, **esbuild 0.28.1**, and `npm audit` now reports **0 vulnerabilities**. Now let me verify the bump didn't break anything: production build, then the E2E suite.

Build passes on vite 7.3.6 (tsc + vite build clean). Now the E2E suite to confirm the dev server and gameplay still work:

All **13 E2E tests pass** and the build is clean. Let me capture the exact diff to report.

## Investigation complete — and a clean fix is ready

**On branch `chore/dependabot-vulns`** (off up-to-date `main`).

### What the 3 alerts actually are
All three are **dev-tooling, Windows-only** issues in the Vite/esbuild build chain — none touch the shipped game (a static client bundle; `vite`/`esbuild` aren't in production output, and they only trigger when running the **dev server on Windows**). So real-world risk for this repo (developed on macOS) is low. Still worth patching for hygiene and to clear the alerts.

| # | Sev | Pkg | Was | Now |
|---|-----|-----|-----|-----|
| 2 | High | vite (`server.fs.deny` bypass) | 7.3.3 | **7.3.6** ✅ |
| 3 | Medium | vite (launch-editor NTLM leak) | 7.3.3 | **7.3.6** ✅ |
| 1 | Low | esbuild (arbitrary file read) | 0.27.7 | **0.28.1** ✅ |

### The fix
The neat part: **vite 7.3.6 widened its esbuild range to `^0.27.0 || ^0.28.0`**, so all three resolve within vite 7.x — no major upgrade to vite 8 and no `overrides` hack needed.
- Bumped `package.json` vite floor `^7.1.7` → `^7.3.6`
- `npm audit fix` pulled esbuild to the patched 0.28.1
- Changes: `package.json` (1 line) + `package-lock.json`

### Verification
- `npm audit` → **found 0 vulnerabilities**
- `npm run build` → clean (tsc + vite build)
- `npm test` → **13/13 Playwright E2E passing**
